decisions.reason: As a multi-model extension of the firm's established geospatial integration offer with its own dedicated page, it likely has strategic fit, low incremental carrying cost, and still-positive option value.

The building digital twin service builds directly on the firm's core geospatial and enterprise-integration capabilities, and after only a short time on the market its uncertainty is not yet resolved enough to justify exit.

This identity-delegation service is close to the core offer and may support broader solution sales, but its more peripheral positioning and overlap risk make it somewhat more disposable than the firm's more clearly embedded products.

An open GIS application framework is strategically important for a German geospatial software firm because it can anchor future projects and variants, so management would usually preserve this option unless results were clearly poor.

The new GIS-focused identity and access service strengthens integration of GeoIT applications into customer environments, and with modest likely carrying costs the firm would typically keep it while market adoption becomes clearer.
